title: Labor on an Open Alignment Plan Work Order — Alignment Services & Plans Rate Manual
content:
**Alignment Services & Plans — labor charged on an open work order of an alignment plan.**

The labor of an open work order is worked out from the visit's work-order date, odometer and alignment type, as follows.

1. **Interval anchor.** The interval anchor of the visit is the plan's latest alignment booked as included in the plan, or the plan's latest alignment booked at the member early price when that one is later and the line's member early price counts toward the interval.
2. **Interval reached.** The interval is reached when at least the line's interval in months — whole calendar months — has passed from the anchor's date to the visit's date, or when the visit's odometer is at least the line's interval in miles above the anchor's odometer, whichever comes first. Whole calendar months are counted to the same day of the month.
3. **Pricing base.** The pricing base of the visit is 0.00 when the interval is reached, and the line's member early-alignment price otherwise.
4. **Labor charged.** The labor charged is the pricing base rounded to the nearest cent and never below 0.00.

The interval figures and the member early-alignment price are those of the plan's line on the product's member interval schedule.

### Worked example (hypothetical plan and figures)

Suppose a plan line with an interval of 6 months or 6000 miles and a member early-alignment price of 70.00 (an illustrative figure, not a line price). The plan's latest included alignment was on 10 January at 40000 miles; a later member-early alignment does not exist.

| Visit | Whole months from anchor | Miles above anchor | Interval reached? | Labor charged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 May at 43100 miles | 3 | 3100 | No | 70.00 |
| 9 July at 44000 miles | 5 | 4000 | No | 70.00 |
| 10 July at 44000 miles | 6 | 4000 | Yes — months | 0.00 |
| 2 May at 46000 miles | 3 | 6000 | Yes — miles | 0.00 |

If instead a member-early alignment on 1 March at 41000 miles were the latest alignment and the line's member early price counts toward the interval, the anchor would move to 1 March and 41000 miles; a visit on 2 May at 46500 miles would then be 2 whole months and 5500 miles from the anchor, the interval would not be reached, and the labor charged would be 70.00.
